Package com.radiantlogic.iddm.util

Class ValidationUtils

java.lang.Object
com.radiantlogic.iddm.util.ValidationUtils
public final class ValidationUtils extends Object
Provides argument validation methods that throw appropriate exceptions for invalid inputs.

This class offers methods to validate method arguments and object state, throwing specific exceptions (IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException, etc.) when validation fails.

The validation approach used here separates validation from casting/retrieval operations. Instead of combining type checking and casting in a single method, this design uses:

  1. A validation step using requireArgument(boolean, String, String...)
  2. A separate casting/retrieval step performed by the caller

Example usage patterns: 


 // Type validation with manual casting
 Object instance = getFromMap(key);
 ValidationUtils.requireArgument(
     ExpectedType.class.isAssignableFrom(instance.getClass()),
     "Cannot assign %s to %s", instance.getClass().getSimpleName(), "ExpectedType");
 ExpectedType result = (ExpectedType) instance;
 
 // Null checking with retrieval
 String value = map.get(key);
 ValidationUtils.requireArgument(value != null, "Missing required value for key: %s", key);
 return value;

  • Method Details

    • requireState

      public static void requireState(boolean stateCondition, String message, String... params)
      Throws an appropriate exception if a state condition is false.

      This method is intended for indicating when the caller has made a mistake by calling an object's method before some precondition is met (e.g., trying to use an object before it is instantiated) and using different method arguments would not have worked.

      Parameters:
      stateCondition - The result of a boolean expression specifying the required state
      message - A detail message format to be used in any resulting exception
      params - Values to feed into the detail message's format string
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the specified condition is false

    • requireState

      Throws an appropriate exception if a state condition is false.

      message - A detail message format to be used in any resulting exception

    • requireArgument

      public static <T> T requireArgument(Optional<T> optional, String message, String... params)
      Throws an appropriate exception if an Optional is empty, otherwise returns the contained value.

      This method provides a convenient way to validate that an Optional contains a value and extract it in a single operation, with a custom error message if the Optional is empty.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The type contained in the Optional
      Parameters:
      optional - The Optional to check and extract from
      message - A detail message format to be used in any resulting exception
      params - Values to feed into the detail message's format string
      Returns:
      The value contained in the Optional
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the Optional is empty
      API Note:
      This method combines validation and extraction, which differs from the pattern used by other methods in this class. It's provided for convenience when working with Optional values where the validation and extraction steps are tightly coupled.
